name: Shared Rhythm
idea: Four unequal folded faces hold an open gathering space; changing height and spacing suggest shared praise.

meaning.tabernacle: Architectural faces turn around a shared open forecourt.
meaning.praise: Their unequal heights and intervals suggest collective rhythm, rather than a literal instrument.
meaning.relationship: The same faces express both gathering space and rhythm; no separate icon is added.

construction: Four separate flat filled polygons on a 256 × 256 canvas.
Inner-right face remains tallest; outer faces stay lower and the lower edges frame an open forecourt.
The primary preserves the projecting second-face apex from the favored direction.
The compact cut narrows the faces and opens the three intervals for tiny raster sizes, while retaining the small second-face shoulder.
changes: Primary geometry is identical to the favored Review 08 v2, not a fresh redesign.
Two compact premises tested: retain a shortened fold shoulder versus remove it for four simpler facets.
The simpler-facet option was rejected for becoming too bar-like.
The selected shoulder version opens the intervals further, then receives a one-unit upper-left correction on the tall face to remove faint diagonal pixel contact at 16 px.

versions.label: Selected tiny-use cut: pixel interval correction

strengths: Keeps the favored primary silhouette and its welcoming asymmetric arrangement.
A single spatial arrangement carries dwelling and rhythmic expression.
The compact drawing separates all four faces at native 16 and 20 px in both tested renderers.
risks: The primary can still read as a cultural venue, property identity or sculptural architecture.
Praise remains abstract; the mark does not independently identify a Christian church without name/context.
The compact cut feels more disconnected at large sizes and must not replace the primary globally.
Four raster components do not prove semantic recognition or aesthetic quality.
smallSize: Use the primary provisionally from 24 px, preferably 32 px and above for the folded-space reading. Use the compact cut only at 16–20 px: all four faces remain separated, but at 16 px the result is still a tiny abstract cadence; the folded-space construction is clearer at 20–24 px and beyond.

provisionalUsage.primary: 24 px and above; 32 px preferred for spatial reading.
provisionalUsage.compact: Only where constrained to 16–20 px; not for normal avatars or large presentations.
provisionalUsage.print: No physical process-specific minimum established; needs real print, vinyl and embroidery proofs before production.

pixelTest.method: 8-neighbor connected components of alpha coverage. Checked thresholds 1, 32, 64, 128, 192 and 224; alpha1 includes faint antialias fringe pixels.
pixelTest.selectedCompactResult: Four components in both renderers, in positive and reverse, at every tested threshold and size.
pixelTest.primaryResult: At 16 px the primary has three components at alpha128, so it remains unsuitable for that tiny use. At 20 px+ it has four substantial components at alpha128, while faint fringes can still meet.
pixelTest.limitations: Single rendering setup per renderer, whole-pixel aligned, device scale1. Arbitrary subpixel placement, resampling, CSS transforms and printing can change results.

visualInspection: Viewed primary and both initial compact premises at large scale and native 16/20/24/32 positives/reverses. Viewed wider-interval follow-up. Final primary/compact board and native files inspected; component metrics support separation only.
font: No font dependency in the symbol. Board annotations use the repository Noto Sans file only; that is not a wordmark recommendation.
approval: Neither mark, palette, typography nor production rule is final. No RCCG emblem is redrawn or embedded.
